sources.title: OpenAI Codex GitHub releases
sources.takeaway: The release page showed 0.137.0 as the latest stable Codex CLI label while 0.138.0 alpha releases were also visible. THOS should distinguish installed-state receipts from source-drift monitoring and avoid treating prerelease labels as mandatory upgrades.

sources.title: OpenAI Codex GitHub repository
sources.takeaway: The repository remains the primary public surface for Codex installation, release assets, and issue/PR drift. Local preflight receipts should pair repository guidance with live version and help-surface checks.

sources.title: MCP security best practices
sources.takeaway: MCP runners should keep consent, redirect validation, state validation, local-server hardening, least-privilege scopes, and confused-deputy/SSRF/session protections as first-class THOS guardrails.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
sources.takeaway: Prompt injection, sensitive output disclosure, excessive agency, supply-chain exposure, and unbounded consumption justify exact approvals, guard scans, raw-output suppression, and staged-diff review before publication.

sources.title: NVIDIA NVL72 AI Factory reference architecture
sources.takeaway: Validated AI-factory reference designs reinforce a THOS pattern of compatibility maps, network/compute separation, explicit runbooks, and repeatable validation receipts rather than ad hoc helper sprawl.

sources.title: NVIDIA AI factories
sources.takeaway: AI-factory planning emphasizes orchestration, power/cooling/compute/networking integration, and simulation-backed design. THOS can translate that into source-led runner topology and dry-run rehearsal rather than hardware claims.

sources.title: Inside the NVIDIA Vera Rubin Platform
sources.takeaway: Rack-scale accelerator roadmaps support the GMUT/THOS practice of separating aspirational compute metaphors from verified local capabilities and measurable validation surfaces.

sources.title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform scaling documentation
sources.takeaway: Agent runtime, sessions, memory, evaluation, tracing, sandboxing, identity, gateways, and policy controls map cleanly onto THOS multiplexer design, with every mutation guarded by explicit approval.

carry_forward_rules: Prefer primary sources over raw search volume.
Treat live version receipts and public release pages as complementary but different evidence classes.
Keep connector and web work read-only unless a later exact packet grants mutation.
Translate security sources into concrete approval, guard-scan, and raw-output boundaries.
Keep all GMUT empirical, physics, consciousness, and canon gates open.
